hypothesis: The FM is currently trained with pointwise BCE on individual (user,video) rows, but both evaluation metrics (GAUC, nDCG@5) are computed within-user, pairwise/ranking-based — a mismatch between training objective and eval objective. Switching to a pairwise BPR-style loss (Rendle et al. 2009), where for each positive (long_view=1) row we sample a negative (long_view=0) row from the *same user's* other impressions and train the model to score the positive above the negative, directly optimizes intra-user ranking correctness instead of absolute calibration. This is a training-procedure/negative-sampling change only (same FM architecture, same FIELDS), so it should isolate whether loss-objective mismatch — not model capacity or features — is the current bottleneck, especially given last iteration's overfitting signature suggests we should be looking at how the model is trained/regularized rather than adding more capacity/features right now.
expected_effect: GAUC should move more than nDCG@5, since BPR's pairwise loss directly optimizes the same intra-user pairwise ordering that GAUC measures, whereas nDCG@5 additionally weights position-within-top-5 which BPR treats all pairs identically regardless of rank position.
